Title: Boulder City Council Special Meeting - July 13, 2023
Overview: The council held a special meeting covering a Parks and Recreation Month declaration, a consent agenda, and public hearings on the New Vista High School site development plan and the 4401 Broadway concept plan for a mixed-use creative campus with a new Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art, with no formal approvals taken on those items. In matters from the mayor and council, members discussed unifying competing ballot measures on extending the 0.15 sales tax, and directed staff to prepare a 50/50 alternative split between arts and the general fund, and agreed to defer board and commission vacancies to the 2024 annual recruitment.

Topic1.Title: Parks and Recreation Month Declaration
Topic1.Summary: Council recognized July as Parks and Recreation Month, and Parks and Recreation staff reflected on departmental achievements, including record free-access program visits and upcoming projects such as Violet Park. Council thanked staff for their work. No vote was required beyond the agenda amendment.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic2.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda, consisting of items 2A through 2C, by unanimous voice vote after a motion and second.

Topic3.Title: New Vista High School Site Development Plan Review
Topic3.Summary: Council held a public hearing to review and comment on the Boulder Valley School District's site development plan to replace New Vista High School with a roughly 74,000 square foot two-story building, new sports field, and reconfigured parking and access. Staff explained the review is per state statute and no approval or denial was taken. The district presented changes made since May, including 18 fewer parking spaces, 64 bike stalls, added EV charging, a sidewalk link, and a revised athletic field approach. Council members praised the responsiveness, asked about construction waste, cross-laminated timber, geothermal grants, and an accessible multi-use path from the east, and a resident urged the project proceed quickly.

Topic4.Title: 4401 Broadway Concept Plan Review
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for a roughly 107,250 square foot mixed-use North Boulder Creative Campus including a new Boulder Museum of Contemporary Art, 67 residential units, retail, and studio space, requiring a 29-space parking reduction and several code modifications. Staff explained the museum use is prohibited in the MU-2 zone and live-work units are prohibited in RM-1, so rezoning, a North Boulder subcommunity plan update, and likely a flex zone would be needed. Council members were generally supportive of the museum use, the land use change path, and the project's consistency with comprehensive plan goals, and asked the applicant to address liquor licensing near the school, the land donation value, and displacement of existing tenants. Council also discussed a possible referral to the Design Advisory Board and Transportation Advisory Board, with the applicant to decide timing, and asked that bike and pedestrian safety be coordinated with Community Cycles.

Topic5.Title: Unification of Arts and General Fund Sales Tax Ballot Measures
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented polling by Probolsky Research showing about 70 percent support for extending the 0.15 percent sales tax, with a 62 percent approval rating for city services. Council discussed a compromise proposed by petitioners of the arts ballot measure to split the 0.15 percent tax 50/50 between arts and the general fund, which would roughly double arts funding. Members debated the trade-offs, the dedicated-funds concern, the 1.8 million dollar existing arts allocation, and legal options. Seven members directed staff to prepare a 50/50 alternative ballot measure for next week, and staff was asked to conduct outreach to bipoc and lower-income arts organizations before final decisions.

Topic6.Title: Midterm Board and Commission Vacancy Recruitment
Topic6.Summary: Staff reported that 12 applications were received for 12 vacancies, with several boards receiving no eligible applicants and interviews completed by council members. Council discussed whether applicants could be placed on other boards and whether the recruitment should be extended. A majority of council, seven members, directed staff to defer unfilled vacancies to the 2024 annual recruitment, which will be prepared beginning in September 2023.
